--- order: 2 unit: page introduces: [js-event] assumes: [js-query, text-content, style-prop] title: "Click events" summary: "Run a function when someone clicks a button: addEventListener, and the difference between handing over a function and running it." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 12 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "", zoom: 1.4} caption: "A click runs a function you hand to addEventListener" say: "A click runs a function you hand to add Event Listener." clip: - caption: "A heading to change, and a button to click." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "

Ready?

\n\n", append: true} - caption: "A function holds the change. Writing it does not run it." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "\n", append: true} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 750 - caption: "Nothing has changed: the page is waiting for a click." - wait: 400 - click: {selector: "#go", preview: true} - expect: {selector: "#message", contains: "Go!", preview: true} - caption: "The click ran start, and the heading changed." - wait: 750 hook: "A page that only changes when it loads is a poster. A page that changes when you click is an app." --- Until now your script ran once, as the page loaded. To react to a click you give the button a **function** and say when to run it: ```js button.addEventListener("click", start); ``` Read it as "when this button is clicked, run `start`". `"click"` is the **event**. The function after it is the **handler**. **The hard part** is the brackets. `start` hands the function over to be run later, on each click. `start()` runs it **right now**, once, and hands over whatever it returned, so the click does nothing. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict check: type: predict q: "What does the heading say when the page first loads, before anyone clicks?" options: ["Ready?", "Go!", "Nothing", "An error"] actual: "Ready? The function start is only run when the button is clicked. Loading the page just tells the button what to do later." ``` Which line decides when `start` runs? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I clicked both buttons and saw the heading change each time." } ``` Press **Run**, then click **Start** and **Pause**. The heading changes only when you click. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "addEventListener hands a function to the browser to run later, on each event; writing the function name with brackets runs it now instead." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each piece with what it does." pairs: - ["function start() { … }", "a recipe for the change: nothing happens until it is run"] - ["goButton.addEventListener(\"click\", start);", "when the button is clicked, run start"] - ["\"click\"", "the event: what the browser waits for"] - ["message.textContent = \"Go!\";", "the change itself, inside the handler"] - check: type: question q: "Which line makes start run on every click?" options: ["goButton.addEventListener(\"click\", start);", "function start() {", "const goButton = document.querySelector(\"#go\");", "message.textContent = \"Go!\";"] answer: 0 explain: "The listener line tells the browser to run start on each click. The function on its own is just a recipe." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "This page says Go! as soon as it loads, and clicking does nothing. There is no red error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 9 fault: logic misconception: call-not-pass explain: "start() has brackets, so it runs at once, when the page loads. Hand the function over without brackets: addEventListener(\"click\", start)." ``` ### Which part does what? Match code with meaning. ### What makes it run? One line decides. ### Spot the bug No error, and nothing works. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Each button needs its own function and its own listener; a handler can change more than one thing." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } tasks: - hint: - "A third button needs three things: the button in the HTML, a function, and a listener." - "Add ``, a function reset that puts back \"Ready?\", and resetButton.addEventListener(\"click\", reset)." expected: page.html#sol-reset check: { type: code, text: "Add a Reset button that puts the heading back to Ready?", rules: { contains: ["id=\"reset\"", "Ready?"] } } - hint: - "A handler can change more than one thing. What else about the heading can you change?" - "Add message.style.color = \"green\"; inside start, and another colour inside pause." expected: page.html#sol-colour check: { type: code, text: "Make Start turn the heading green and Pause make it orange.", rules: { contains: [".style.color"] } } ``` ### A reset button Back to the beginning. ### Colours A handler can change two things. ## Make: buttons of your own ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: at least two buttons that change different things, each with its own function." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I made a page with at least two buttons that each change something different." } ``` Start from the two buttons and make a page where each button changes something different: size, colour, words, or a picture. The page on this lesson makes a heading bigger, smaller or purple. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "A page needs to count clicks. What does the handler need to keep between clicks?" options: ["A variable made outside the function", "A new variable made inside the function each time", "A second button", "Nothing: the browser counts"] answer: 0 explain: "A variable made inside the function starts over each click. A variable made above it keeps its value. Lesson 6." ``` You can now run code on a click. Next: change how the **whole page looks** with classes. ```teacher summary: Students run a function when a button is clicked with addEventListener, tell handing over a function from running it, fix a listener written with brackets, add a Reset button, and make buttons that change different things. time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can run a function when someone clicks a button. - I can say what the event name and the handler are. - I can give a handler without running it straight away. before: > Read the unit primer first. This is the Python events lesson (a handler runs when something happens) in JavaScript, and the same lesson as p5's `mousePressed`, but the page picks the element and the event. `addEventListener("click", start)` hands the browser a function; `start()` calls it now. The bug has no red error, so students must look at the page: it says Go! straight away. Functions were taught in the p5.js course; if students skipped it, spend a minute on "a function is code with a name" first. IDs named like variables (`message`) are fine here because the script uses `const`. running: - "Predict: ask what is different between writing a recipe and cooking it." - "Run: ask students to click each button and say which function ran." - 'Investigate: for the bug, ask "when did the heading change, and why then?"' - "Modify: ask where the third button is in the HTML, and where in the script." - "Make: ask each pair which button does what, before they test." stuck: - see: The heading says Go! at once and the button does nothing. ask: Are there brackets after start in the listener? fix: 'Remove them: addEventListener("click", start).' - see: Cannot read properties of null (reading addEventListener). ask: Does the button id in the HTML match the selector? fix: "Match the id exactly, with # in the selector." - see: Nothing happens when I click. ask: Did you press Run, and is the button inside the page? fix: Press Run again; check the id. - see: The new button does nothing. ask: Did you add a listener for it? fix: Add its listener under the others. stretch: Make one button toggle between two states using a variable, or make a button remove itself with button.remove(). support: Give the whole Reset function and listener, and ask students to change what it says. leads: "Next lesson: classes, to change how the whole page looks with one line." exit: q: What is the difference between start and start() in a listener? a: start hands the function over to run on each click; start() runs it once, right now. explain: > 1. `addEventListener("click", start)` says: when this button is clicked, run `start`. 2. `start` has no brackets because we hand over the function, not run it. 3. The handler changes the page each time the event happens. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-reset step-4#t2: page.html#sol-colour step-5: page.html#sol-make struggle: "Brackets: start hands the function over, start() runs it now. The page, not an error, shows the slip." ```
